citation: Gilbert, K.M. and Shi, Q. Interpretable ensemble machine learning for flood susceptibility mapping in Lagos Lagoon, Nigeria.
predictors_used: Ensemble ML (interpretable), SHAP explainability, unsupervised clustering into 5 susceptibility zones
validation_data: Topography, hydrology, spectral (NDVI etc.), climatic, socioeconomic factors
stated_gap_or_limitation: Harmonized Sentinel-1 SAR flood mask (2024), 20,000 balanced samples
how_this_project_differs: Produces a susceptibility surface, not an infrastructure-condition or road/drainage-specific outcome; does not include primary field verification of infrastructure state
column12: This project uses primary field-verified road/drainage infrastructure vulnerability as the target, at the site level rather than a regional grid, with independent field validation instead of relying solely on remote-sensing-derived labels

citation: Akindejoye, A., Viavattene, C., Priest, S. and Windridge, D. Identifying social vulnerability profiles for coastal flood using supervised and unsupervised machine learning: a case study of Lekki Peninsula, Lagos, Nigeria.
journal: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
methods: Supervised + unsupervised ML profiling of social vulnerability
stated_gap_or_limitation: Focuses on social/household vulnerability profiles, not the physical condition or flood response of road and drainage infrastructure itself
how_this_project_differs: This project targets infrastructure vulnerability (road and drainage condition/exposure), which is conceptually and empirically distinct from household social vulnerability; the two are complementary but answer different questions

citation: Aniramu, O., Odelola, R., Okebugwu, J., Ojimadu, U. and Orimoogunje, O. Integrating hydro-climatic drivers, flood frequency, and dynamic perception for sustainability assessment of flood vulnerability in Lagos, Nigeria.
spatial_scale: 5 Lagos LGAs (Ajeromi/Ifelodun, Eti-Osa, Kosofe, Lagos Island, Surulere)
methods: Mixed-method: hydro-climatic trend analysis, flood frequency (Log-Pearson III/GEV), CHIRPS rainfall mapping, Likert-scale perception survey, binary logistic regression, Dynamic Flood Sustainability Index
predictors_used: Rainfall trend, streamflow, drainage density, elevation, income, education, previous flood experience, early warning access
validation_data: Ground rainfall + CHIRPS + streamflow (1983-2023), household questionnaire
stated_gap_or_limitation: Rainfall/hazard-and-perception focused; drainage is only a self-reported household perception variable (Likert score), not a directly measured physical infrastructure condition; no road-segment-level or engineering assessment of drainage/road state
how_this_project_differs: This project directly measures physical road and drainage infrastructure condition in the field (not perception or self-report) as the primary outcome, at the level of individual road segments rather than household or LGA aggregates

citation: Olotu, T.O., Oyewo, S.T. and Omoniyi, O. Impact of Seasonal Flooding on Flexible Pavement Performance in Southwestern Nigeria.
spatial_scale: Lagos, Oyo and Ogun States (multiple road sites)
methods: Field surveys, Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) testing, geotechnical/CBR lab testing, multivariate regression predicting Pavement Condition Index (PCI) from flood variables
predictors_used: Flood duration/intensity, CBR, FWD deflection, subgrade condition
validation_data: Field deflection testing and lab CBR testing (primary), no independent remote-sensing or ML validation layer
stated_gap_or_limitation: Closest existing comparator: it is infrastructure-level and field-based like this project, but it is a pavement-engineering study without a drainage-specific field protocol, without stratified citywide sampling across flood-exposure zones, and without any ML-based predictive modelling, SHAP interpretability, or spatial cross-validation
how_this_project_differs: This project adds a standardized combined road+drainage field protocol, stratified citywide sampling (not project-by-project road sections), and an ML prediction/interpretability layer validated against remote-sensing flood evidence, which this pavement-engineering study does not attempt
